svg.title: How to play - setup, the weekly pulse, and the end (A4 portrait)
svg.desc: A4 quick reference. Everything needed to sit down and play, on one side of paper. Black and white line art for cheap office printing; styling comes later.
svg.text: HOW TO PLAY
Seven weeks. Five days a week, for the whole team. Six features. One deadline that does not move.
ONE NEW IDEA A WEEK - THE BOARDS UNCOVER THEMSELVES
SETTING UP
about fifteen minutes, and the first part is the best part
1 · DEAL EVERYONE A CHARACTER - BEFORE ANY RULE IS EXPLAINED
Deal each player five parts at random, one from each row of the habitus sheet, and assemble the figure: Base → Legs → Torso → Head → Item.
You are handed a habitus, not asked to choose one - nobody picks their upbringing. Slot the cards into the seats on your person board.
Take your Base's Knowledge card. Ninety seconds, no decisions, and everyone has touched the game.
2 · LEAVE THE OTHER BOARDS FACE DOWN, AND CHOOSE THE PROJECT
Only board 1 starts face up. Boards 2 and 3 stay text side up; the Specimen strips stay in the box until week 4.
Put one Project card in its seat; it names features A - F. LOCK tiles across D and F. Out come Work, Coordinate, Celebrate.
3 · SET THE STARTING VALUES
Motivation 3 for every character (three tokens in the five wells). Week marker on Week 1. Shuffle the Events but don't draw yet.
Everything on the covered boards already sits at 2. It just isn't your problem for two more weeks.
THE PULSE OF A WEEK
seven times, then it's over
1 · PLAN THE WEEK
Lay five Activity cards across Monday to Friday. Put a character disc on each - that person's Skill,
Knowledge and Capital apply to that day. One person may take several days, or none. A slot may instead
take a Flex marker, giving back a day someone worked as Overtime. Then stop. Nothing has resolved.
2 · SHIT HAPPENS
Draw two Event cards, face up - and do not resolve them yet. They are threats, not facts. They are aimed at
the week you have already committed, which is the point. A day spent on the wrong thing is simply lost.
3 · ADAPT
Spend [Adaptability]: each 1 replaces one card, or pays an Event's ADAPT number to cancel it outright.
4 · THE WEEK RUNS
Resolve whatever survived Adapt, then all five cards. Order does not matter - the week happened at once.
Total it up and move the counters. There is no separate resolution step.
5 · CLOSE THE WEEK
Bank completed features (lift any lock, pay Capital) → walk the Ledger coins, at most one step each, and
flip any that reached its ring → Motivation as one net number: lose 1 to the grind, +1 if the Need was met.
bank first - it pays the capital the ledger needs.
apply motivation as one number, then check for zero.
HOW IT ENDS
the project ends when Week 7 closes
TEAM SCORE = (features × 10) + (four track values) + (Motivation), LESS 5 PER QUIT AND PER UNREPAID FLEX
FAILURE
Not everything delivered.
The score doesn't matter.
HEROIC SUCCESS
All six banked, score under 80.
The project made it. The team didn't.
HIGH PERFORMANCE
All six banked, score 80+.
You built a team as well.
If you only had thirty-five working days, how would you spend them?
